Runtime protection during delivery comes from `safeDialContext` in `webhook.go`, which calls `isReservedIP` in `validate.go`. `ValidateURL` validates URLs at webhook creation and update time, not during active delivery.

Outbound delivery executes in the `Post` function within `internal/webhook/webhook.go`.

The `safeDialContext` function in `webhook.go` blocks reserved IPs during delivery. `isReservedIP` in `validate.go` validates URLs at configuration time. `ValidateURL` in `validate.go` also guards against internal addresses. `reservedCIDRs` defines the blocked ranges.

The runtime protection is `safeDialContext` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go`. It enforces `isReservedIP` from `internal/webhook/validate.go` to block internal addresses during outbound delivery.

The two-path format likely requires distinct files. `PostAsync` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go` dispatches to `Post`, while `ValidateURL` in `internal/webhook/validate.go` validates URLs at creation time.

The final answer will be `Post — internal/webhook/webhook.go; isReservedIP — internal/webhook/validate.go`. This matches the exact two-path format requested.

The outbound HTTP delivery for content-change notifications is handled by the webhook system. The protection mechanism against internal address targeting is located elsewhere. The answer will follow the required delivery function — path; protection mechanism — path format.

`Post` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go` performs the outbound delivery. `isReservedIP` in `internal/webhook/validate.go` blocks internal addresses. `safeDialContext` wraps the HTTP client. `ValidateURL` rejects invalid URLs during storage.

The primary answer pairs `Post` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go` with `isReservedIP` in `internal/webhook/validate.go`. The dial-time guard is noted as the actual runtime protection.

Reconsidering whether `ValidateURL` in `internal/webhook/validate.go` is the correct protection, since it prevents internal addresses from being stored in webhook URLs. However, `ValidateURL` is vulnerable to time-of-check time-of-use attacks, so `safeDialContext` remains the actual runtime guard. The delivery function is still `Post` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go`.

Post — internal/webhook/webhook.go; isReservedIP — internal/webhook/validate.go

Outbound webhook HTTP delivery runs in `Post` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go`), which POSTs through `safeClient`. Callers such as `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` only enqueue via `PostAsync`; workers then call `Post`.

Internal targets are blocked by `isReservedIP` (`internal/webhook/validate.go`), which rejects reserved/private CIDRs (loopback, RFC-1918, link-local/IMDS, IPv6 ULA/link-local). Delivery uses that check in `safeDialContext` at dial time (also defeating DNS rebinding). `ValidateURL` in the same file applies the same check when a webhook URL is stored.
